info.name: Supervised-scope matrix (Slice A - ADR 0029)
info.description:
A unit manager who is a member of NO team sees the catalogs of the teams their reports own or manage - read-only, live, and derived entirely from the reporting structure, never from a realm grant. Asserted on EXACT ids and counts through the gateway.

Runs in ORDER. E4 is deliberately LAST: it mutates the reporting edges (the declarative bootstrap replace) and every earlier cell depends on the original org.

TWO FOLDERS, TWO PASSES. 'Matrix' is E1-E6/E9/E10 on the normal rig. 'Supervised-edge outage' is E8 and needs a SECOND short pass with only CATALOG_USER_SERVICE_SUPERVISED_BASE_URL repointed at a dead port - see run-supervised-scope-matrix.sh.

item.name: Matrix
E1 — HEADLINE: sup-anna (member of NO team) GET /catalogs -> exactly her unit

exec: pm.test('E1 200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
const ids = body.items.map(i => i.id);
// Exact ids AND an exact count - not just a status code. Anna is a member of NO team, so
// every row here came from the reporting structure and nothing else.
pm.test('E1 anna sees EXACTLY 3 catalogs', () => pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(3));
pm.test('E1 anna sees her direct reports\' catalogs (bob, carol)', () => {
pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.environment.get('bob_catalog_id'));
pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.environment.get('carol_catalog_id'));
pm.test('E1 TRANSITIVITY: her report\'s report\'s catalog (dave, via carol) is included', () =>
pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.environment.get('dave_catalog_id')));
pm.test('E1 REACH RULE: a report\'s READER seat does NOT propagate', () =>
pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.environment.get('reader_catalog_id')));
pm.test('E1 anna does NOT see the adjacent unit (victor\'s)', () =>
pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.environment.get('erin_catalog_id')));
pm.collectionVariables.set('anna_ids', JSON.stringify(ids.sort()));

item.name: E2 — sup-victor GET /catalogs -> a DISJOINT set

exec: pm.test('E2 200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
const ids = body.items.map(i => i.id);
pm.test('E2 victor sees EXACTLY his unit (1 catalog)', () => {
pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(1);
pm.expect(ids).to.eql([pm.environment.get('erin_catalog_id')]);
const annaIds = JSON.parse(pm.collectionVariables.get('anna_ids'));
pm.test('E2 the two units are DISJOINT - neither leaks into the other', () =>
ids.forEach(id => pm.expect(annaIds).to.not.include(id)));

item.name: E3 — outsider-eve (neither member nor supervisor) -> empty page, 200

exec: pm.test('E3 200 OK - not 403, not 500', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.test('E3 the wire count is 0 (the empty-page floor, ADR 0012)', () => pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(0));
pm.test('E3 no items', () => pm.expect(body.items.length).to.eql(0));

item.name: E10 — the realm marker ALONE: unit-supervisor claim + ZERO reports -> empty page

exec: pm.test('E10 200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
// The realm role is a UX-only eligibility marker, never resolver input (ADR 0029). This subject
// carries it and supervises nobody, so it must grant NOTHING - the distinction from the
// realm-role fallback slice B4 deliberately removed.
pm.test('E10 the claim grants nothing: count 0', () => pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(0));
pm.test('E10 no items', () => pm.expect(body.items.length).to.eql(0));

item.name: E5a — read-only ceiling: anna GET a supervised catalog -> 200

exec: pm.test('E5a anna may READ a supervised catalog (200)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: E5b — anna PUT the supervised catalog -> 403

body.raw: {"name":"anna should not be able to rename this","description":"nope"}

exec: pm.test('E5b update is DENIED (403)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: E5c — anna PUT with a TAGS delta (the assign-tags dispatch) -> 403

exec: // A catalog's tags are assigned through PUT; the update handler's delta dispatch turns a tags
// change into an assign-tags decision (ADR 0022). Either way the supervised ceiling denies.
pm.test('E5c tag assignment is DENIED (403)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: E5d — anna DELETE the supervised catalog -> 403

exec: pm.test('E5d delete is DENIED (403)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: E5e — the _actions affordance on a supervised row: present, view-only

exec: pm.test('E5e 200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const row = pm.response.json().items.find(i => i.id === pm.environment.get('dave_catalog_id'));
pm.test('E5e the supervised row is on the page', () => pm.expect(row).to.not.be.undefined);
// PRESENT, not omitted: the omit-on-all-false degrade fires only when EVERY verb is false,
// and `view` is true here. The verb set is the shipped CatalogEnrichable registry.
pm.test('E5e _actions is PRESENT, not omitted', () => pm.expect(row._actions).to.not.be.undefined);
pm.test('E5e view:true', () => pm.expect(row._actions.view).to.eql(true));
pm.test('E5e update:false', () => pm.expect(row._actions.update).to.eql(false));
pm.test('E5e delete:false', () => pm.expect(row._actions.delete).to.eql(false));
pm.test('E5e assign-tags:false', () => pm.expect(row._actions['assign-tags']).to.eql(false));

item.name: E6a — CONTENTS OPEN (slice B): anna lists the supervised catalog's categories -> 200

exec: // FLIPPED BY SLICE B (PRODUCTION-TIER), deliberately and in that slice's own plan. In slice A the
// synthesized role named no `category` key, so this was a 403 — the boundary of A. B widens the
// role to name the child types (a DIRECT grant; ADR 0031's inheritance confinement is untouched)
// and gates the read on the governing root's `env` tier instead. This catalog is UNTAGGED, which
// ADR 0030 §3 defines as non-production, so contents OPEN.
// The closed-contents proof did not vanish — it MOVED to run-production-tier-matrix.sh, which owns
// the production cells (401 + the RFC 9470 challenge, since slice C flipped B's plain 403) and
// the tier-flip liveness cell; the unproven/absent state closes at the module layers (the rego
// absent-clause tests + the enrichment IT's outage cases).
pm.test('E6a the category LIST is OPEN (200)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.test('E6a exactly the seeded category, by id', () =>
pm.expect(body.items.map(i => i.id)).to.eql([pm.environment.get('dave_category_id')]));
pm.test('E6a and the count agrees', () => pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(1));

item.name: E9 — DUAL-HAT: pm-carol is BOTH a member and a supervisor of one catalog

exec: pm.test('E9 200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
const dave = pm.environment.get('dave_catalog_id');
const ids = body.items.map(i => i.id);
// carol governs Sup Carol Co (administrator) and Sup Dave Co (owner); she ALSO supervises
// Sup Dave Co through her report pm-dave. supervised := S \\ M removes it from the supervised
// leg, so the row is judged by her MEMBERSHIP role and appears exactly once.
pm.test('E9 the doubly-reachable row appears EXACTLY ONCE', () =>
pm.expect(ids.filter(id => id === dave).length).to.eql(1));
pm.test('E9 the authorized total counts it once (2, not 3)', () => pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(2));
const row = body.items.find(i => i.id === dave);
// MEMBERSHIP WINS: her owner seat's affordances, NOT the supervisor role's read-only ceiling
// (which E5e pinned as update:false on this very same catalog).
pm.test('E9 the row carries the MEMBERSHIP role\'s affordances (update:true)', () =>
pm.expect(row._actions.update).to.eql(true));

item.name: E4a — LIVENESS: remove pm-bob from anna's reports (declarative replace)

exec: // The removal seam is a DECLARATIVE POST: the posted set REPLACES the manager's whole edge set,
// so omitting pm-bob removes that edge (STATUS-01's decision).
pm.test('E4a the reporting edges were replaced (200)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: E4b — anna re-lists: pm-bob's catalog is GONE on the very next request

exec: pm.test('E4b 200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
const ids = body.items.map(i => i.id);
pm.test('E4b bob\'s catalog is gone - the derivation is LIVE, not cached', () =>
pm.expect(ids).to.not.include(pm.environment.get('bob_catalog_id')));
pm.test('E4b carol\'s branch survives (carol + dave = 2)', () => {
pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(2);
pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.environment.get('carol_catalog_id'));
pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.environment.get('dave_catalog_id'));

item.name: E4c — and the withdrawn catalog is genuinely DENIED, not merely hidden

exec: // The list hiding a row and the gate denying it are two different guarantees. This is the
// second one: revoking the edge withdraws ACCESS, not just visibility.
pm.test('E4c a direct GET of the withdrawn catalog is 403', () => pm.response.to.have.status(403));

item.name: Supervised-edge outage
E8a — supervised edge faulted: anna sees ONLY her own memberships (none) - never all catalogs

exec: // Failure class 1 (00-DESIGN): an errored/unreachable org source degrades the subject to their
// OWN MEMBERSHIPS. Anna is a member of no team, so that floor is the empty page.
pm.test('E8a 200 OK - no 5xx leaked out of the faulted edge', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
const body = pm.response.json();
pm.test('E8a anna degrades to her own memberships: count 0', () => pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(0));
pm.test('E8a and certainly not the whole table', () => pm.expect(body.items.length).to.eql(0));

item.name: E8b — the fault is CONFINED to the supervised edge: a member's page is unchanged

exec: // This is what the DEDICATED supervised base-URL buys. Role resolution and tag definitions
// still run against the real user-service, so pm-carol's membership page is untouched. Had the

pm.test('E8b 200 OK', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

pm.test('E8b carol still sees both her governed catalogs', () => pm.expect(body.count).to.eql(2));
const ids = body.items.map(i => i.id);
pm.test('E8b the ids are carol’s and dave’s', () => {
pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.environment.get('carol_catalog_id'));
pm.expect(ids).to.include(pm.environment.get('dave_catalog_id'));
